theme: No single record of an account
underlying structural problem: Case history, status, and activity are split across disconnected tools, so staff must reconcile manually.
why it matters now: Higher handling cost and slower throughput from manual reconciliation and workaround effort.
top repeated sub-signal example quote: The audit trail is scattered across email, spreadsheets, and the legacy database, making compliance reviews a nightmare.

underlying structural problem: No control point enforces callback dates, ownership handoffs, or contact sequence discipline.
why it matters now: Delayed or missed customer contact reduces recovery speed and increases preventable leakage.
top repeated sub-signal: contact timing and progression visibility gaps
top repeated sub-signal example quote: The scale of the problem means that even small improvements in efficiency multiply significantly.

underlying structural problem: Status semantics and activity logging are inconsistent, so reporting outputs are not decision-grade.
why it matters now: Leaders cannot trust performance numbers, weakening planning, forecasting, and governance decisions.
top repeated sub-signal example quote: The data quality is so poor that we stopped running management reports altogether.

theme: Customers cannot see or settle their own case
underlying structural problem: Customers do not get clear balance/status visibility or clear routing between self-service and assisted paths.
why it matters now: Customer friction and confusion lower resolution rates and undermine portal adoption.
top repeated sub-signal example quote: Customers go through the contact process multiple times because we have no way to prevent re-contact.

theme: Risky cases are not separated from straightforward ones
underlying structural problem: Triage does not reliably separate vulnerable/specialist-risk cases from straightforward recoveries.
why it matters now: Inadequate triage raises complaint risk and compliance exposure in sensitive edge cases.
top repeated sub-signal: risk attribution and decisioning is unclear
top repeated sub-signal example quote: We have no way to tell whether a customer is genuinely unable to pay or simply avoiding contact.

theme: Agents and managers may not adopt it
underlying structural problem: Change delivery lacks trust, readiness, and clear benefit ownership, so adoption is at risk.
why it matters now: Low adoption risk can erode expected benefits even if technical delivery succeeds.
top repeated sub-signal example quote: We need to fix the fundamentals before we can build anything new on top.
